title: Quantum vs Classical Cryptography
description: One-time pads, RSA, Shor and Grover, and information-theoretic security

questions.question: In classical cryptography, the main task of an encryption algorithm is to
options: were measured in any basis, with mismatched ones later corrected by Alice
completely random, while the pair's joint results are strongly correlated
convert a plaintext into a ciphertext that cannot be read without the key
a source that sends one photon of each pair to Alice and the other to Bob
questions.correctAnswer: convert a plaintext into a ciphertext that cannot be read without the key

questions.question: The Vernam one-time pad achieves perfect secrecy only if
options: the key is a secret but short string that is easy to distribute
the key is derived from the plaintext with a secure hash function
leaves the state as the original superposition, but now with a known value
the key is truly random, at least as long as the message, and never reused
questions.correctAnswer: the key is truly random, at least as long as the message, and never reused

questions.question: Why is the one-time pad perfectly secure?
options: the four states are not mutually orthogonal, and a measurement that distinguishes non-orthogonal states inevitably disturbs them
with ideal devices the observed correlations are the entangled ones, so a departure from them can only come from outside interference
every plaintext of that length is consistent with the same ciphertext, so the ciphertext carries no information about the plaintext
A qubit can be a coherent superposition of $|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle$, whereas a classical bit is always exactly $0$ or exactly $1$
questions.correctAnswer: every plaintext of that length is consistent with the same ciphertext, so the ciphertext carries no information about the plaintext

questions.question: The main practical weakness of the one-time pad is
options: It conveys that the lack of response was deeply meaningful.
private, so that Eve cannot read the announced bases at all
their security follows directly from the no-cloning theorem
the difficulty of distributing a key as long as the message
questions.correctAnswer: the difficulty of distributing a key as long as the message

questions.question: Frequency analysis breaks classical substitution ciphers because
options: proof that a message was sent by a particular sender and has not been altered
the ciphertext preserves the statistical frequencies of the plaintext symbols
ordinary optical amplifiers can restore the photon count without adding noise
quantum mechanics can never be verified experimentally to arbitrary precision
questions.correctAnswer: the ciphertext preserves the statistical frequencies of the plaintext symbols

questions.question: Public-key cryptography solves a problem that symmetric cryptography cannot solve by
options: an eavesdropper cannot impersonate one of the two parties during the public exchange of bases and error data
allowing two parties to establish a shared secret over a public channel, with no prior private key exchange
The theorem applies to arbitrary unknown superpositions, not to states that are already known basis states
predictable basis choices would let an adversary know which measurements to make in order to avoid detection
questions.correctAnswer: allowing two parties to establish a shared secret over a public channel, with no prior private key exchange

questions.question: The security of RSA rests on
options: authenticated, so that Eve cannot impersonate Alice or Bob during sifting
the practical difficulty of factoring a large product of two large primes
convert a plaintext into a ciphertext that cannot be read without the key
$|0\rangle$ with probability $1/2$ and $|1\rangle$ with probability $1/2$
questions.correctAnswer: the practical difficulty of factoring a large product of two large primes

questions.question: Which statement about RSA key sizes is correct?
options: the ability to initialise, manipulate and read out qubits, together with isolation from the environment
larger moduli make factoring harder, which is why recommended RSA key sizes have grown over the decades
chain of repeaters that each share entanglement with their neighbours to extend entanglement end to end
testing whether the observed correlations violate a Bell inequality for more than one pair of settings
questions.correctAnswer: larger moduli make factoring harder, which is why recommended RSA key sizes have grown over the decades

questions.question: Shor's algorithm threatens public-key cryptography because it
options: factors large integers and computes discrete logarithms in polynomial time on a quantum computer
hashes the remaining bits so that Eve's information about them is reduced to a negligible amount
they are physically equivalent, since every measurement outcome probability is identical for both
close the locality and detection loopholes, otherwise the violation can be explained classically
questions.correctAnswer: factors large integers and computes discrete logarithms in polynomial time on a quantum computer

questions.question: Grover's algorithm improves unstructured search over $N$ candidates by
options: reducing the number of queries to a polynomial in $N$
reducing the number of queries from about $N$ to about $\sqrt{N}$
increasing the number of required queries by a factor of $\sqrt{N}$
abort the run, since the key bits can no longer be assumed secret
questions.correctAnswer: reducing the number of queries from about $N$ to about $\sqrt{N}$

questions.question: If Grover's algorithm is applied to a $k$-bit symmetric cipher key, the effective brute-force security becomes
options: roughly $2^{k/2}$ candidate keys, i.e. about $k/2$ bits of security
roughly $2^{2k}$ candidate keys, i.e. $2k$ bits of security
were measured in the basis matching the one in which they were sent
the impossibility of generating random numbers quantum mechanically
questions.correctAnswer: roughly $2^{k/2}$ candidate keys, i.e. about $k/2$ bits of security

questions.question: The usual response to Grover's algorithm is to
options: replace random keys with a fixed key agreed once and used forever
The school reduced its electricity purchases after installing solar panels.
double the symmetric key length, for example moving from AES-128 to AES-256
must measure in one of the three bases, which changes the sifted key length
questions.correctAnswer: double the symmetric key length, for example moving from AES-128 to AES-256

questions.question: A cipher is said to be information-theoretically secure when
options: two non-orthogonal bases are needed, so that no measurement can identify the basis without introducing detectable errors
any attempt to gain information about a quantum state disturbs it, and the disturbance appears as errors in the shared key
the information an eavesdropper can obtain is bounded by a computable quantity no matter how much computing power is used
its security can be established from observed correlations alone, without trusting the internal operation of the devices
questions.correctAnswer: the information an eavesdropper can obtain is bounded by a computable quantity no matter how much computing power is used

questions.question: In its ideal form, quantum cryptography differs from classical public-key cryptography because its security
options: information-theoretic, resting on the laws of quantum physics rather than on computational hardness
produces one definite outcome, and the state after the measurement is the corresponding basis state
follows from the laws of physics rather than from the current difficulty of a computational problem
must interact with the entangled photons, which breaks the correlations tested by Bell's inequality
questions.correctAnswer: follows from the laws of physics rather than from the current difficulty of a computational problem

questions.question: A quantum channel allows something a classical channel cannot, namely
options: proved that a quantum state can be copied with fidelity above the classical limit
The result is always $|0\rangle$, because a superposition forces the zero outcome
transmitting a quantum state whose measurement statistics can reveal interception
Both are reversible, so any measurement can be undone by applying a Hadamard gate
questions.correctAnswer: transmitting a quantum state whose measurement statistics can reveal interception

questions.question: A QKD system actually produces
options: destroys the state so completely that no further measurement is possible
the plaintext message itself, delivered without any classical cipher
every experiment that tests Bell's inequality must support local realism
a shared secret key, which the users then use with a conventional cipher
questions.correctAnswer: a shared secret key, which the users then use with a conventional cipher

questions.question: In QKD, the classical channel is required to be authenticated so that
options: allowing two parties to establish a shared secret over a public channel, with no prior private key exchange
predictable basis choices would let an adversary know which measurements to make in order to avoid detection
The theorem applies to arbitrary unknown superpositions, not to states that are already known basis states
an eavesdropper cannot impersonate one of the two parties during the public exchange of bases and error data
questions.correctAnswer: an eavesdropper cannot impersonate one of the two parties during the public exchange of bases and error data

questions.question: Why is QKD expected to resist attacks by future quantum computers while RSA does not?
options: left unauthenticated, since the quantum channel already provides authentication
Four: $|\Phi^+\rangle$, $|\Phi^-\rangle$, $|\Psi^+\rangle$ and $|\Psi^-\rangle$
computational, resting on the difficulty of a problem such as integer factoring
QKD security is based on physical principles rather than computational hardness
questions.correctAnswer: QKD security is based on physical principles rather than computational hardness

questions.question: Which statement about the difficulty of integer factoring is correct?
options: a random choice from three bases, two of which supply the key and one of which is used for the Bell test
no polynomial-time classical algorithm is known, but Shor's algorithm provides one on a quantum computer
deploying hybrid classical and post-quantum key exchange, so security holds if either scheme is unbroken
photons cannot be amplified without adding noise, so losses must be compensated by entanglement swapping
questions.correctAnswer: no polynomial-time classical algorithm is known, but Shor's algorithm provides one on a quantum computer

questions.question: Quantum computers threaten the Diffie-Hellman key exchange through
options: brute force over a small number of pre-shared values
Shor's algorithm applied to the discrete logarithm problem
measurement-induced collapse of the shared secret
the sifted key must be regenerated at every few kilometres
questions.correctAnswer: Shor's algorithm applied to the discrete logarithm problem

questions.question: Post-quantum cryptography differs from quantum cryptography because it
options: The experiment was repeated three times, each trial produced slightly different results,
the assumption that a cryptographic hash function has no practical preimage or collision
runs on ordinary computers using classical algorithms designed to resist quantum attacks
The experiment was repeated three times; each trial produced slightly different results.
questions.correctAnswer: runs on ordinary computers using classical algorithms designed to resist quantum attacks

questions.question: A source of true unpredictability is essential in quantum key generation because
options: predictable basis choices would let an adversary know which measurements to make in order to avoid detection
allowing two parties to establish a shared secret over a public channel, with no prior private key exchange
The theorem applies to arbitrary unknown superpositions, not to states that are already known basis states
an eavesdropper cannot impersonate one of the two parties during the public exchange of bases and error data
questions.correctAnswer: predictable basis choices would let an adversary know which measurements to make in order to avoid detection
